claims.text: Conventional cast CoCrFeNiTi has coarse grains, significant porosity, and lower hardness.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi elemental powder mixture has coarse grains and high porosity.
The initial material exhibits a thermodynamically unstable FCC solid solution prone to HCP precipitation.
High-energy ball milling for approximately 6 hours followed by SPS is an applicable synthesis route for CoCrFeNiTi.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling produces sufficient dislocation density, lattice strain, and grain refinement in CoCrFeNiTi.
Milling-induced strain lowers the activation-energy barrier for a metastable FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transition.
VEC and atomic-radius mismatch govern the FCC/BCC phase-stability window in Ti-rich CoCrFeNiTi.
The 6-hour milling treatment avoids Ti-driven HCP nucleation because it does not allow sufficient nucleation time.
SPS at 1000°C supplies sufficient diffusion and thermal energy to densify ball-milled CoCrFeNiTi.
Rapid SPS under uniaxial pressure for less than 15 minutes is compatible with powder-processed high-entropy alloys.
At 1000°C, SPS remains below the threshold for excessive grain coarsening and extensive Ti-rich HCP precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
The combined treatment produces a fine-grained, dense single- or dual-phase BCC/FCC microstructure.
The processed alloy will have less than 2% porosity.
The processed alloy will have a grain size below 1 micrometer.
The processed alloy will exceed 600 HV and be significantly harder than its cast counterpart.
The hardness increase will arise primarily from grain-boundary and solid-solution strengthening rather than HCP precipitation.
Sintering above 1050°C triggers excessive grain growth and Ti-rich HCP or Laves-phase precipitation.
Precipitation above the proposed temperature boundary degrades ductility and changes the dominant hardness mechanism to brittle precipitation hardening.
Low-load HV0.1 testing can isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.
Failure to exceed 500 HV, formation of more than 5 vol% HCP phase, or retention of more than 5% porosity is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The starting material is described simultaneously as an elemental powder mixture and as an FCC solid solution; an unalloyed elemental mixture is not yet the asserted FCC solid solution.
